Flood Insurance Data

NFIP flood claims by county: how often they get paid

Of 267,368 NFIP flood claims for losses from 2020 on, 83.4% had a recorded payment. In the 68 counties with 500 or more such claims, the share runs from 52.7% in Terrebonne Parish, LA to 94.4% in Somerset County, NJ.

83.4%
Claims with a recorded payment, U.S., losses 2020 on
267,368
NFIP claims counted

FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP Claims v3, as of August 31, 2026. A recorded payment is any building, contents or Increased Cost of Compliance payment above $0. Left out: 15,438 records FEMA coded "Claim deleted in error" or "Assigned in error"; counted as claims with no payment, the U.S. share would be 78.8%. FEMA's data does not say whether a claim is still open, so a recent claim with no payment may still be paid.

Filing an NFIP flood claim: proof of loss and rebuilding costs

Already flooded? Insured: report the loss to your insurance agent or company now (FEMA's steps: how to start a flood claim), and send a proof of loss (your signed, sworn statement of the amount you are claiming) within 60 days of the flood (44 CFR 61, App. A(1), Art. VII). Not insured: a policy bought today will not cover a flood that already happened, and FEMA disaster aid is open to people in counties designated in a federally declared disaster.

Under the NFIP's rules, a building is substantially damaged when restoring it to its condition before the damage would cost 50 percent or more of its market value before the damage (44 CFR §59.1). An NFIP policy with building coverage pays up to $30,000 under Increased Cost of Compliance to comply with a state or local floodplain law when repairing a flood-damaged building.

Of the 2,069,464 NFIP claims with a recorded payment for losses from 1978 to 2026, all 50 states and DC, 41,384 (2.0%) include an Increased Cost of Compliance payment.

FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP Claims v3. A recorded payment is any building, contents or Increased Cost of Compliance payment above $0; records FEMA coded "deleted in error" or "assigned in error" are left out. Puerto Rico and the other territories are not in these totals. FEMA's data has no open or closed field, so counts for recent loss years are not final. NFIP claim appeal deadlines are with the other program rules.

How big is a typical paid claim?

Across the 50 states and DC, the median paid building claim is $12,384, on 1,968,497 claims. By state, the median paid building claim runs from $2,998 in Montana to $21,899 in Louisiana, among the 49 states with 500 or more such claims (left out, with fewer: District of Columbia, Wyoming).

Median of the building payment on claims with recorded building damage and a building payment, every loss year since 1978, in dollars as paid, not adjusted for inflation. Contents payments are not in it. Each state page shows its own figure.

What these numbers cannot tell you

No recorded payment does not mean a claim was denied: it includes damage under the deductible, claims not pursued and reasons FEMA does not record. These are shares of claims filed, not a chance that any one claim gets paid.
